c8.text: The filter optimizer accepts tuples above the upper proxy threshold, rejects tuples below the lower threshold, and sends intermediate tuples to the oracle model.
c8.quote:
If the tuple’s proxy score is at least𝜏+, we mark it as pass-
ing the predicate. If the tuple’s proxy score is less than or equal to
𝜏−, we mark it as failing the predicate, and for tuples with proxy
scores between 𝜏+ and 𝜏−, we resort to the oracle model to provide
a label.
c8.review_reason: The operation matches the described threshold rule, but the source includes equality at both thresholds while the assertion does not specify those boundary cases.

c32.text: The BioDEX task uses 65,000 biomedical articles and 24,000 possible drug-reaction labels.
c32.quote:
task on the BioDEX Dataset [ 29], which consists of a corpus of
65, 000 biomedical articles, and ground-truth expert-created drug
safety reports constructed from each article. The task is to classify
the patient’s drug reactions, given each medical article. Notably,
there are 24, 000 possible drug-reaction labels, making this task an
extreme multi-label classification task.

c35.text: The BioDEX outcome metrics are rank-precision at 5 and rank-precision at 10.
c35.quote:
The table reports the rank-precision@5 (RP@5) and
rank-precision@10 (RP@10), following prior work [ 28], as well
as execution time in seconds and the number of LLM calls.

c48.text: Across the two ranking tasks, the authors report 16% to 32% lower execution time for quick-select top-k than heap top-k, without mapping the range endpoints to a task in the prose.
c48.quote:
Notably the quick-select top-𝑘 offers 16 − 32% lower execution
time than the heap-based sorting method, despite requiring more
LLM calls in some cases.
